Thank you for contacting us regarding the south lift at Elara Residences, 88 Kavanagh Street, Southbank.

We are sorry to hear the south lift has been out of service since Friday and understand this is particularly difficult given your mother's mobility needs, as well as being the third outage in a short period.

If the situation changes or there is any further deterioration (for example, the north lift also becomes unavailable), please contact us immediately.

Kind regards,
Fictional Strata Partners Pty Ltd
Owners Corporation Manager – Elara Residences (PS612884K)

A lift outage since Friday with a mobility-impaired person in the affected lot constitutes a safety and accessibility risk that is materially worsening with each day, warranting urgent classification. No specific lift rule was retrieved so none are cited; the maintenance obligation falls under the OC's general duty to maintain common property. No committee decision is required to chase the contractor — that is a day-to-day management action — but the recurring failure pattern should be flagged to the committee.

Dear F. Fictional,

Thank you for getting in touch regarding Lot 4 at Craigieburn Rise (22 Hanson Road, Craigieburn).

We are sorry to hear about the leak from your dishwasher. Under Rule 2.4 of the Craigieburn Rise Owners Corporation rules, repairs within a lot — including internal plumbing fixtures and appliances — are the responsibility of the lot owner and are not the responsibility of the owners corporation. Accordingly, the owners corporation is unable to arrange or fund a plumber to attend to this matter on your behalf.

We would encourage you to engage a licensed plumber as soon as possible to stop the leak and assess any resulting damage to your flooring, as prompt action will help prevent the situation from worsening.

If it is established that the leak has caused any damage to common property, please notify us in writing and we will assess the matter further in accordance with Rule 2.2.

Kind regards,
Fictional Strata Partners Pty Ltd
Owners Corporation Manager — Craigieburn Rise (SCH003)
rows.reasoning: The dishwasher and internal plumbing fixtures fall squarely within the lot owner's maintenance responsibility under Rule 2.4. The owner is not in arrears and occupies the lot. There is no common property involvement indicated, no safety risk to another person, and no legal or financial deadline, so urgency is routine.

rows.draft_reply:
Dear Owner of Lot 103,

Thank you for writing to us again about this matter. We understand your frustration, and we want to assure you that your concerns are taken seriously.

The conduct you describe — a dog off lead in the lobby, and animal waste left unattended near the lift — appears to be inconsistent with the rules of Elara Residences. In particular:

• Rule 5.2 (Animals on common property) requires that dogs be kept on a lead on common property at all times, and that owners immediately remove and dispose of any animal waste.
• Rule 2.1 (Use of common property) prohibits use of common property in a way that unreasonably interferes with another person's use and enjoyment of it.

As this is a repeat complaint, we will be referring the matter to the committee for their consideration and direction on next steps, which may include issuing a formal breach notice to the owner of Lot 12. The committee will need to authorise any enforcement action before we can proceed.

We will update you once the committee has provided its direction. Thank you for your patience.

Kind regards,
Fictional Strata Partners Pty Ltd
Owners Corporation Manager — Elara Residences (PS612884K)
rows.reasoning: This is a repeat rules-breach complaint about an identifiable lot. Rules 5.2 and 2.1 are clearly applicable. Because the complaint has been raised at least twice before, the matter should be escalated to the committee for a direction to issue a formal breach notice; the manager cannot authorise that unilaterally. There is no immediate safety emergency, so urgency is routine.
